                                   PUC DOCKET NO. 58481

      RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                   §
      LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                §
      STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561             §     PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF
                                                §                 TEXAS
                                                §


    HUT 8 CORP’S COMMENTS ON COMMISSION’S PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION


                        PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION OF NEW 16
       COMES NOW Hut 8 Corp (HutTAC
                                  8) §25.194
                                      and files these comments in response to the
Commission’s March 12, 2026 Proposal for Publication (PFP) of new 16 Texas Administrative
Code (TAC) §25.194 relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, which sets forth new
standards and criteria for the interconnection of new large load customers to the ERCOT
transmission network.

                        COMMENTS AND PROPOSED CHANGES
Hut 8 makes the following comments and suggests the following changes to the PFP:
   1. Batch Zero Consideration
          Projects that have valid interconnection studies completed and confirmed by ERCOT
          and have funded the costs in aid of construction (CIAC) for all required interconnection
          facilities in accordance with the schedule set forth in the executed interconnection
          agreement with the interconnecting transmission and/or distribution service provider
          (TDSP) should not be subject to any further financial security or collateral posting
          requirements. Projects that have reached these milestones have demonstrated their
          legitimacy and have funded sufficient costs to bear no stranded cost risk to either the
          interconnecting utility or other ratepayers. Additionally, for these same reasons, these
          projects should not be subject to a $50,000 per megawatt (MW) non-refundable
          interconnection fee.
   2. Financial Security
          a. Hut 8 recognizes the need for financial security to eliminate speculative projects
              that are cluttering the queue while protecting ratepayers from stranded costs in the
              event a large load customer withdraws its capacity request. While the proposed
              $50,000/MW in financial security is reasonable in size, the framework for how it is
              held, carried forward and returned or refunded is extremely critical. For example,
    any CIAC payments required and funded under the interconnection agreement
   should be covered out of the required $50,000/MW financial security requirement
   posted at the time the intermediate agreement is executed. Additionally, the
   language in ERCOT Planning Guide Revision Request 145 should be aligned with
   the final rule adopted here with respect to required financial commitments.
b. Hut 8 proposes the following framework for addressing financial commitments
   required of each large load customer:
       i. Pending the interconnection study process under subsection (e), the full
          amount of the $50,000/MW financial security posted at the time the
          intermediate agreement is executed should remain refundable because there
          is not yet any line of sight to the specific capacity amounts and timeline
          available for the project.
      ii. Within sixty (60) days following completion of the interconnection study
          process under subsection (e), the large load customer must decide whether
          to move forward and be included in the transmission plan or withdraw their
          load and receive a full refund.
      iii. If the large load customer decides to proceed, the previously posted financial
          security carries forward and becomes non-refundable only for the amount
          of capacity allocated to the project. The amounts for any requested capacity
          not allocated to the project based on the results of the interconnection study
          would be refunded to the large load customer.
              1. Example: a large load customer files a 1,000 MW interconnection
                  request and posts $50M in security. After the interconnection study,
                  the customer is only allocated 300 MW. Assuming the customer
                  moves forward with 300 MW, $15M of the initial security posting
                  would be credited toward the cost of significant equipment and/or
                  services and CIAC, and the remaining $35M would be refunded to
                  the customer.
c. The non-refundable interconnection fee required under subsection (f)(7) is an
   unreasonably cumulative financial commitment, and there is no clearly defined
   purpose for such fee. It is unnecessary to effectuate the purposes of Senate Bill 6
   and will most likely reduce the level of business development in the state while
   failing to meaningfully reduce the potential for stranded assets or improve system
           reliability. There are sufficient provisions in place in the rule for large load
          customers to provide payments through CIAC for direct interconnection costs and
          to post financial security that will cover the costs of necessary equipment, services
          and system upgrades. These substantial financial commitments should ensure that
          any speculative load requests will be filtered out through the interconnection
          process. Therefore, Hut 8 recommends that the non-refundable interconnection fee
          provision be removed from the PFP.
3. System Upgrade Security
      A separate security should be posted, due at the time of the execution of the
      interconnection agreement under subsection (f), for projects for which the
      interconnection study has identified system upgrades necessary to reliably serve the
      requested load. Upon completion of the interconnection study and identification of any
      necessary system upgrades, the large load customer will be informed of any system
      upgrades necessary to serve their load, along with a timeline for availability of the
      requested capacity. If or when the customer decides to move forward, it will be required
      to post additional security in the amount of the system upgrades, as determined by
      ERCOT. The remainder of this security after satisfying any outstanding amounts owed
      for cost incurred to fulfill the interconnection request should be returned to the customer
      on a pro rata basis over five years upon the large load meeting the requested peak
      demand in each of those years.
4. Interconnection Agreement Timing
      Under the current proposal, a 30-day window is a very tight timeframe for a large load
      customer and an interconnecting TDSP to negotiate and execute an interconnection
      agreement. Hut 8 recommends extending this deadline to a minimum of 60 days to
      allow both parties to obtain internal approvals, conduct thorough document review and
      negotiations, and finalize any required ancillary items, including demonstration of site
      control.
5. Non-Utilized Capacity
      a. The current proposed six-month window for satisfaction of milestones in a
          customer’s schedule for phased energization is too short. The rule should be moved
          to a 12-month buffer for the customer to meet each milestone outlined in the ramp
          schedule. Additionally, the rule should provide that if the customer’s project is
          progressing in good faith and can show proof of continued development, it should
    be left to the discretion of the TDSP as to whether reallocation of the load is
   necessary or appropriate.
b. A portion of the demand included in many large load customers’ schedules for
   phased energization is intended to cover the power necessary to run cooling
   systems. Some requested demand for cooling systems is only necessary when
   seasonal cooling demands are high, which is very temperature dependent.
   Reallocation because of load ramp milestones that are not met due to mild weather
   that did not necessitate operation of the cooling systems is not a good policy.
c. Complete reallocation of a customer’s requested capacity to a different project is
   overly punitive to a customer that has demonstrated financial commitment to both
   ERCOT and incurred significant external development costs, including land rights,
   equipment, and services.
d. Further, the project to which the capacity is reallocated would likely take longer to
   be studied and energize than the project from which the capacity was taken,
   resulting in unreasonable delays in overall business development in the state
   without any corresponding improvement in reliability.
e. In the event a customer’s capacity is reallocated based on a failure to meet an
   energization milestone, ERCOT should apply the posted financial security to any
   outstanding amounts owed and then refund 100% of the remaining balance to the
   customer. The purpose of the security is to prevent stranded costs from being
   socialized to ratepayers. Once these costs have been covered, there is no further
   need for the security, and the remaining balance should therefore be refunded to the
   customer.
                                        CONCLUSION
       Hut 8 appreciates the opportunity to provide comments on the PFP and the Commission’s
consideration of these comments in its development of the final rule in this proceeding.

                                             Respectfully submitted,

                                             /s/ Casey Bell
